judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The newsletter form's text input labelled 'Nome' (id form-field-name_news, label for=) asks the visitor for their own name to subscribe them. In the snapshot (post-script DOM) and in the live HTML fetched today it has no autocomplete attribute, and neither the form nor any script adds one, so the purpose 'name' (a purpose listed in WCAG 2.1 section 7) is not programmatically determined; H98 is the sufficient technique and nothing else on the element stands in for it. Looked for reasons to dismiss: the field is not someone else's data, not hidden, and browser autofill heuristics do not count as programmatic determination. Whether 'Nome' means full or given name only changes the token, not the failure. Live page matches the capture, so the claim names a real 1.3.5 failure.
